Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 38, worksheet line 3: "Are you filing Schedule D? Yes. Enter the smaller of line 15 or line 16 of Schedule D. If either line 15 or line 16 is blank or a loss, enter -0-. No. Enter the amount from Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 7a." With Schedule D the candidate enters the smaller of lines 15 and 16 when both are nonnegative and zero when either is a loss, which is the project's floored smaller. Without Schedule D the candidate enters line 7a floored and the project enters sd.distributions; when sd.filed is false (no sales, no 28% or section 1250 gain) sd.line16 = sd.line15 = sd.distributions and f1040.line7a = sd.to1040 = sd.line16, so the two are equal. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/qdcg.deepseek.json; 1,083 fixtures, 500 generated returns; no partial records, qdcg has no own inputs): all 1,583 comparisons agree (1,469 non-refusing). Project stands.

Ruling: representation; i1040gi p.38 QDCG worksheet line3 uses Form1040 line7a when ScheduleD is not filed; in the supported distribution-only route that amount is sd.distributions, while all direct sales/loss routes require ScheduleD. On the filed route, max(min(SD15,SD16),0) equals min(max(SD15,0),max(SD16,0)), the printed loss-to-zero rule. This compares the prepared, supported-return quantities; it does not claim arbitrary inconsistent supplied cross-form subtotals or all partial-input paths are equivalent.

Ruling: representation; i1040gi (2025) p. 38 QDCGT line 3 requests the smaller Schedule D lines 15/16, zero for a loss, or Form 1040 line 7a when no Schedule D is filed. The two Schedule D branches are equal because max(min(a,b),0)=min(max(a,0),max(b,0)) for all signed amounts (order-preserving max); 40,401 signed pairs around zero also checked. In a supported complete return with sd.filed=false there are no sales or special-rate gains: sd.count, line18 and line19 are zero, carryovers and other non-modeled income are refused. Schedule D lines 7/15/16 reduce to 0/distributions/distributions, so f1040.line7a via sd.to1040 equals the NonNegDollars sd.distributions and its zero floor is identity. This is a completed-return arithmetic proof; no new assertion about unknown/blank partial entries is claimed.

Ruling: representation; archived i1040gi (2025) p. 38 QDCGT line 3 takes the smaller Schedule D lines 15/16, zero for a loss, or Form 1040 line 7a when no Schedule D is filed. The filed-Schedule-D expressions are definitionally equal: subtract_floor0(min(a,b),0) = max(0,min(a,b)). For a supported complete return with sd.filed=false, sales and special-rate gains are absent, carryovers/unmodeled income are refused, and Schedule D lines 7/15/16 reduce to 0/distributions/distributions. Thus f1040.line7a via sd.to1040 equals the NonNegDollars sd.distributions. This is a completed-return arithmetic proof and does not assert equality of partial/unknown-entry evaluation.
